operationMap.puzzleImplication: Prefer physical/visual mirror actions and right-to-left reading before cryptographic transformations.
operationMap.currentStatus: Direct prose reversal and raw hflip have been tested; they identify regions, not final letters.

operationMap.puzzleImplication: A left/right page or left/right side selector remains more plausible than whole-article hashing.
operationMap.currentStatus: 78/79 as two hands is suggestive but first/last and binary selectors failed.

operationMap.puzzleImplication: The strongest live geometry should be treated as a crossing/communication rule between pages, not one page alone.
operationMap.currentStatus: The p79-yellow -> p76-black row anchor fits this concept but lacks extraction unit/order.

operationMap.puzzleImplication: The clue supports reversing the reading direction, but only after the correct source layer and target region are known.
operationMap.currentStatus: Reversing current reflected text streams produced no instruction, so the missing piece is upstream.

assessment: The paper supports mirror/left-right/bimanual concepts, not a named cryptographic transform.
It reinforces the existing page-76 and 76/79 orientation model.
It still does not specify source layer, ordering, or extraction unit.
Future tests should require a fully stated human rule before generating candidates.
